Anya Rao: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a few clarifying Qs on release cadence, oncall handoffs, and quality gates. TL;DR: where do we land on weekly vs biweekly releases for infra and customer-facing APIs?
Mike Chen: Short answer: infra -> weekly deployments by default, customer-facing APIs -> biweekly mainline releases. Exceptions possible for critical patches. We'll publish a schedule this week.
Laura Patel: Can we get a written playbook for oncall handoffs? Yesterday's 2am swap was confusing — missing who owned the long-running incident.
Sam (Eng Ops): Yep. Working on an "oncall-handbook.md" in engops repo. Draft by EOD Friday. It will include: handoff checklist, escalation matrix, and runbook links.
Chris: Who owns the SLA targets per model route? Is that product or runtime?
Anya Rao: Runtime owns latency/availability SLAs (service level objectives at infra-level), Product owns business SLAs (e.g., error rates that impact customers). Runtime will provide a per-route latency budget doc and a mapping to product SLAs.
Mike Chen: For quality bars: required items before any rollout >= major version: unit tests, perf benchmarks, evals passing threshold, and a canary rollout plan. Canary must include pre-defined eval prompts and observability hooks.
Laura Patel: Do we have a defined rollback / canary window? e.g., canaries for 2 hours then auto-promote if healthy?
Sam (Eng Ops): Default canary policy we propose: min 1h, max 12h. Auto-promote if errors = 0 and latency within threshold for the window and no regression alerts. Manual promote allowed if team signs off. Policies can be overridden per-release.
Devex Bot: Links: https://redwood.internal/engops/oncall-handbook  |  https://redwood.internal/roadmap/release-schedule
Anya Rao: I'll synthesize this thread into a one-pager and link the playbook in #eng-ops. Leadership — can we commit to a quarterly review of these defaults (canary windows, cadence, SLA ownership)?
Mike Chen: Yes — propose first review in 3 weeks, I'll slot it in leadership cadence and invite relevant owners.
Chris: +1. Also can someone capture escalation numbers and primary contacts? Need the pager rotations in the doc.
Sam (Eng Ops): Pager rota is in the handbook draft. I'll add a simple table and a sample handoff template. Example handoff message: `Handing off oncall -> @Mike Chen. Open incidents: #123 (model OOM), #127 (routing flake). Runbooks: /runbooks/model-oom.md`
Laura Patel: Please add a short checklist for regression evals that ties to PRs (e.g., evals must run and pass before merge on model changes).
Anya Rao: Great. If no objections I'll mark action items and file the doc.
Mike Chen: No objections. :+1:
